frames.narration: A 70-billion-parameter model in 16-bit form needs 140 GB for its weights. One 80 GB GPU cannot hold it.
The quantizer picks a scale: the largest weight, 0.9, divided by 127, which is 0.00709.
Each weight is divided by the scale and rounded: 0.12 becomes 17, -0.5 becomes -71 and 0.9 becomes 127.
Only the small integers and the scale are stored: one byte per weight instead of two. The memory for the weights halves.
While serving, each integer is multiplied back by the scale. 17 becomes 0.1205, close to the original 0.12. The largest error here is 0.0031.
If one huge weight had set the scale, all the others would be squeezed into a few levels. That is why outliers need care, and why quality must be measured.
